onboarding.welcome.lede: {appName} is local-first: your conversations, attachments, and artifacts stay on this machine. Provider credentials live in the OS keychain — never in plain settings. recovery.delete.backupOnly.body: Removes the {backupSize} backup of the store that failed to upgrade. Your fresh store and settings are not touched, and no restart is needed.
recovery.delete.backupOnly.bodyUnknownSi: Removes the saved backup of the store that failed to upgrade. Your fresh store and settings are not touched, and no restart is needed.

recovery.delete.panel.title: Delete local data
recovery.delete.wipe.body: Applied on the next launch — the database is held open while {appName} is running, so the delete happens at startup. {appName} restarts immediately.
recovery.delete.wipe.confirmLabel: I understand this cannot be undone.
recovery.delete.wipe.scopeConversationsL: Conversations, attachments, artifacts, and backups. Your settings and API keys are kept.
recovery.delete.wipe.scopeEverythingLabe: Everything above plus settings, logs, and diagnostics — back to a first run. API keys stay in your OS keychain either way.

recovery.discardBackup.deleted: Deleted {count, plural, one {# backup file} other {# backup files}}, freeing {freed}.

recovery.header.hint: You can continue right now with the fresh store — everything works, it is just empty. Restarting re-runs the upgrade from scratch, which is worth one try if the failure was transient. If you would rather not keep the backup, delete it below.
recovery.header.lede: A database migration failed at startup. To keep the app usable, {appName} started with a fresh local store. Your previous data was backed up before the reset — it is untouched and you can recover from it manually.
recovery.header.title: {appName} could not upgrade your local data

settings.diagnostics.disclosure.body:
{appName} diagnostics export includes:
  • active provider + model
  • local-only flag, diagnostics-enabled flag, theme
  • redacted app paths (your home folder prefix is stripped)

It NEVER includes:
  • secrets or API keys
  • provider base URLs
  • artifact remote allowlists
  • conversation or message content

The bundle is written to your local exports folder.
settings.diagnostics.disclosure.title: Diagnostics export disclosure
settings.diagnostics.header.title: Diagnostics
settings.diagnostics.intro: A diagnostics bundle contains your active provider/model, flags, theme, and redacted app paths. It never contains secrets, base URLs, allowlists, or conversation content.

settings.privacy.keychainMode.fileBody.a: environment variable — a base64-encoded 32-byte value — and is never written to disk beside the file it protects. Without that variable set, {appName} cannot read or save keys in this mode and will say so rather than falling back to the keychain. This is weaker than the OS keychain and is intended for machines that have none, such as headless CI.

settings.privacy.keychainMode.osBody: Keys live in the operating system’s keychain, guarded by your login session. Switch to the file store only on a machine without one — it is a weaker posture, and switching does not move keys you have already saved.

settings.webSearch.allowedDomains.help: One bare domain per line (no http(s) prefix). Max 100 entries. Leave empty for unfiltered search.

settings.webSearch.consent.autoItem: Auto — provider-hosted when available; otherwise the configured local backend.
settings.webSearch.consent.hostedItem: Provider — queries go to the model provider’s hosted search (OpenAI, Gemini, or Anthropic). Each call may incur provider cost.
settings.webSearch.consent.intro: When you turn on web search, the model can look things up on the internet during this conversation. Where the query goes depends on Settings → Web Search → Search source:
settings.webSearch.consent.localItem: Local — {appName} searches from this machine using the backend you pick in Settings (DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Brave, or SearXNG). Queries are not sent to the model provider.

settings.webSearch.externalWebAccess.hel: Unchecked = cache-only / offline mode. Provider ignores this for some models.
settings.webSearch.hostedOnlyNotice: Provider search options apply only when the search source resolves to provider-hosted.
settings.webSearch.includeSources.help: When on, the provider returns the raw source list alongside citations. May increase response size.
settings.webSearch.includeSources.label: Show source list in search results

settings.webSearch.userLocation.heading: Approximate user location

settings.workspaceTools.consent.title: Enable workspace file tools?

settings.workspaceTools.intro: Bind a folder from the chat bar (“Work in a folder”) for a single conversation. Use this section for a default folder on new chats. Sensitive filenames stay blocked; {appName} does not expose a shell.
